items.description: Contact Center historical analytics provides out-of-box historical reporting for Dynamics 365 Contact Center, built on a shared analytics foundation. It moves reporting from heavier workload-specific Power BI models toward a shared analytics foundation with conformed facts, shared dimensions, pre-built aggregations, and common definitions across conversations, sessions, agents, queues, channels, CSAT, handle time, and operational KPIs. Customers can continue using out-of-box Power BI reports while gaining extensibility through Fabric, Direct Lake, SQL, Spark, and custom lakehouse models.

items.title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Shared analytics for historical reporting
items.description: Dynamics 365 Customer Service provides out-of-the-box historical reporting built on a shared analytics foundation: a scalable, open, and AI-ready data foundation for Customer Experience and AI analytics scenarios across Dynamics 365. It uses a lakehouse-based architecture that can scale with data volume, supports curated analytics datasets for direct querying, and enables consistent reporting and semantic definitions across reports, agents, and copilots.

items.title: Microsoft Purview: Data Lifecycle Management-Legacy Teams retention policies covering Copilot will be treated as Teams-only
items.description: Some existing retention policies scoped to Microsoft Teams may currently also apply to Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions. As part of an upcoming change, these legacy Teams retention policies will be converted to—and treated as—Teams-only policies. They will no longer implicitly govern Copilot workloads.

items.title: Microsoft Edge: Ask Copilot about an image

items.title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Envision and design AI agents in Business Central
items.description: AI agents in Business Central Business Central introduces AI agents to help users automate repetitive tasks and make business processes more intelligent and efficient. These agents act as specialized assistants that understand context, handle structured data, and collaborate with users to complete end-to-end workflows. For example, the Sales Order Agent simplifies order creation by transforming natural language or email instructions into complete sales documents, while the Payables Agent streamlines vendor invoice processing by extracting key details from incoming invoices and matching them to purchase orders—all reducing manual effort and freeing users to focus on higher-value work. The agent runtime that powers these built-in agents provides core capabilities that enable the use of agentic AI within Business Central. AI agents are defined, configured, activated, and run directly inside the familiar Business Central environment—leveraging the same security model, administration tools, and user experience as the rest of the product. Results are displayed in-context, with intuitive navigation to related data and entities, allowing users to control the agents through the interface they already know. This consistency dramatically reduces the learning curve, builds trust, and ensures efficiency when working with AI agents. The agent runtime ensures that every step taken by an agent is traceable and operates strictly within the access boundaries (permissions) assigned during configuration. It provides a timeline view of all agent activities, allowing users to review what happened and why—enabling a true human-in-the-loop experience. The runtime can also memorize relevant data during execution, use it in subsequent steps, and request additional instructions in natural language when user input is needed. It helps ensure that sensitive operations always require explicit user review and consent, supporting full transparency and control. Business Central business processes are inherently multistep, stateful, and financially consequential. The agent layer must be able to interact with a broad set of ERP capabilities and data, sequence operations with a high degree of accuracy across dependent steps, handle the data respecting permissions, company, environment, and tenant boundaries, provide a contextual audit trail, and keep humans in the loop. Business Central agentic strategy intentionally separates deep, well controlled, in-context and transparent execution within the product from cross-system orchestration. Business Central agents form the foundational layer inside the product, exposing well-defined agent capabilities that in the future will be possible to surface as MCP tools and consume by Declarative Agents in Microsoft Copilot Studio and Microsoft 365. This layered approach enables Business Central-tuned, transparent, managed execution at the ERP core processes, while allowing higher-level Declarative Agents to orchestrate end-to-end business processes across products. Designing agents The new in-product experience for designing agents that automate Business Central processes is made available with AI Development Toolkit for Business Central. The experience offers a low-risk environment for envisioning and prototyping new AI agents tailored to your own business scenarios—extending the same agent runtime capabilities used by built-in Business Central agents. Built for rapid iteration, the designing experience lets you create and refine custom agents using natural language instructions, define their behavior, test agent profiles and permissions, and safely experiment with Business Central data in a sandbox environment. This approach empowers partner personas like consultants, product owners, and domain experts, as well as developers and even power users, to explore new scenarios, validate ideas, and build confidence in their agents before moving to production. Whether you aim to automate repetitive business processes, streamline data processing, or deliver proactive insights, the agent design experience gives you the tools to bring your vision to life. Agent instructions At the core of every agent are its goals and instructions, defined in natural language. Writing agent instructions is similar to writing prompts for large language models, so you can apply general prompt-writing best practices—and even use tools like Copilot to optimize them. The agent design experience includes a simple editor to help you define, refine, and test these instructions efficiently. Invoking your agent You can invoke your agent by manually creating a task for it. When doing so, you can include an additional message that provides specific details or context to complement the agent’s core instructions. Although the ability to design your own agents is in public preview, there aren't yet any built-in integrations to automatically trigger these custom agents based on incoming emails, events, or scheduled recurrences (this can be done by professional developers using the APIs available in the AI Development Toolkit). However, you can simulate these scenarios by including the email header and body in the task message to mimic incoming emails, or by manually triggering the agent to emulate event, UI action, or time-based runs. Troubleshooting When running the agent tasks in the designing experience, you can access detailed diagnostic views to help you understand and tune the agent execution. Since an agent’s decisions depend on its instructions, available data, and language model reasoning, you can review execution logs to see its inputs, reasoning process, and outputs. This helps you identify where uncertainty occurred and why specific decisions were made to adjust your agent instructions. Importing and exporting agents To make it easy to back up or move custom agents across sandbox environments, the in-product experience allows you to import and export agent definitions. These definitions are stored as simple JSON files containing properties such as agent identity, instructions, assigned profiles, and permissions. We recommend storing these files in a source control system like GitHub to track changes and maintain version history. Responsible AI Agents built using the agent design experience adhere to Microsoft’s Responsible AI principles, helping you ensure agent compliance, fairness, and safety. Billing As with the built-in Sales Order and Payables agents, custom agents consume Copilot credits as they perform their steps. Credits can be provisioned through prepaid or pay-as-you-go models, providing flexible cost management as your AI usage scales. Business Value: Agents in Business Central are AI-powered team assistants that go beyond traditional automation. Unlike static workflows or hard-coded AL logic, agents can interpret high-level business goals expressed in natural language and translate them into actionable steps. They reason over Business Central data, make informed decisions within defined boundaries, and collaborate with users through human-in-the-loop approvals for critical operations. The benefits are substantial: agents reduce manual effort by automating repetitive or complex tasks, allowing users to focus on higher-value activities. They adapt to dynamic business scenarios that can't always be anticipated during development, offering flexibility that traditional automation lacks. Most importantly, agents operate transparently: every action is logged, permissions are rigorously enforced, and users remain in control at all times. This combination of intelligence, adaptability, and accountability makes agents a cornerstone of the next generation of ERP experiences. With the agent design experience, we're taking the first steps toward enabling you to build your own custom Business Central agents. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

items.title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: Copilot and agents - Use AI resources for your Copilot extensions
items.description: Using the AI resources provides several benefits: Reduced operational overhead : Avoid the need to handle infrastructure management, updates, monitoring, troubleshooting, or maintenance of custom Azure OpenAI subscriptions. This benefit frees up resources to focus on core business operations and provides value-adding intellectual property (IP) to customers. Simplified onboarding : Quickly integrate AI capabilities into your solutions without having to navigate the complexities of setting up and managing your own Azure OpenAI subscription. Improved reliability : Proactive scaling, throttling, load balancing, and fault tolerance measures ensure consistent performance during peak demand. Enhanced security compliance : Built-in compliance measures and governance, including robust protection from malicious and harmful content, ensure compliance with data residency requirements. This benefit reduces the burden of ensuring regulatory compliance for ISVs. Streamlined experience for customers : Customers get a seamless AI resource management process without maintaining different configurations for separate ISV solutions. This capability also provides a cohesive AI consumption tracking and billing experience for Business Central customers. Customers who use AI resources across multiple AI-enabled solutions built with Business Central customer developer tools for Copilot benefit from a unified approach to AI consumption monitoring and invoicing. They don't need to reconcile multiple invoices or metrics from separate ISVs. For details on billing costs, see AI tools at Message scenarios . For most publishers, the default Business Central AI resources are enough. However, if you need specific models, including fine-tuned models, that the Business Central AI resources don't provide, you can bring your own subscription for customers. In this case, the publisher is responsible for deploying, maintaining, scaling, and securing the service. The publisher also handles billing AI resources to customers. We recommend using the developer toolkit AI resources when you extend Copilot in Business Central. You just need to authenticate with the SetManagedResourceAuthorization method in the AI Module AzureOpenAI codeunit. You also provide your own Azure OpenAI subscription details, but the authentication process doesn't use them. (Update 2026 release wave 1: There's now a new method signature for SetManagedResources that doesn't require you to provide your subscription details anymore. You should use that going forward.) // Example of using the default toolkit AI resources in AL AzureOpenAI.SetManagedResourceAuthorization(Enum::"AOAI Model Type"::"Chat Completions",AzureOpenAIAccountName,AzureOpenAIApiKey,AOAIDeployments.GetGPT4oLatest()); To use your own subscription, authenticate it with the SetAuthorization method. // Example of using your own Azure OpenAI subscription in AL AzureOpenAI.SetAuthorization(Enum::"AOAI Model Type"::"Chat Completions",GetEndpoint(),GetDeployment(),GetApiKey()); This AI billing model isn't designed to replace the existing Marketplace monetization pathway for publishers who create Business Central apps. Instead, it offers another option that simplifies AI consumption for customers and partners. ISVs can use the Marketplace monetization option to monetize their IP. Business Value: A key feature of the developer tools for Copilot in Business Central is that publishers in their Marketplace apps use large language models through Microsoft-managed Azure OpenAI resources when they extend Copilot in Business Central. This approach eliminates the need for customers to independently get and manage Azure OpenAI subscriptions. Using the Business Central AI resources is the default and recommended approach. However, some partners or customers might have special requirements that require them to use their own Azure OpenAI subscription when running the feature in production or when developing and testing in sandboxes, which is also supported in the developer tools for Copilot in Business Central. items.title: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Data: Agents and Copilot - Increase AI accuracy by grounding agents in customer insights
items.description: The Customer Insights MCP server allows AI agents and chat experiences to access and understand insights generated by Customer Insights - Data. The Customer Insights MCP server uses the industry-standard MCP architecture to securely share unified profiles and insights with AI agents and chat experiences, providing the data context so AI agents can do their best work. AI tools can use the Customer Insights MCP server to: Resolve Dataverse contacts and leads to their unified customer profile. Access extended customer information unified by Customer Insights - Data from external sources not available to Dataverse. Understand calculated measures for a customer such as their purchase totals over the last 4 months, or the date of their most recent engagement. Quickly discover what segments the customer is a member of. See if a customer has multiple redundant contacts in your system, and which is considered authoritative for that customer. Get predictive insights for the customer such as Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) and Churn risk, giving you greater insights into the customer's current relationships with your company. Scenario Sally is a seller who is evaluating a lead named Joe who recently attended a product launch webinar. Sally asks her AI embedded on their Contact and Lead forms if there are any insights about this lead and is delighted to find that the lead Joe is matched to a VIP customer Joseph who has existing paid licenses for several products. Because Customer Insights - Data unifies her company's external Purchase and Rewards data with Dataverse contact and lead data, the agent informs Sally that Joe is a valued Rewards and Loyalty points member, and it is able to provide other AI-generated insights such as the Customer Lifetime Value score, Churn Risk, and the segments Joe is a member of. Armed with a wealth of customer data, Sally is able to engage Joe and upsell Joe on their new product. Business Value: Agents give your marketing, sales, and service teams essential insights and can automate many business processes. But agents are only as good as the data they work with. When you give them access to customer insights that unify your customer data sources, you can get more valuable and actionable insights that enable organizational efficiencies that you couldn't achieve before. Now, more insights generated by Customer Insights - Data can be leveraged from within Microsoft Copilot Studio, allowing you to turn insights into a powerful business asset. Copilot Studio, and even your own custom copilots created in Microsoft Copilot Studio, can now simply and easily get access to more insights, allowing agents to understand, share, analyze, and act on these insights. Every team member gets tailored information and tools to reach their goals efficiently. Enabled for: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

By combining guided setup, continuous review, and contextual recommendations, the security agent helps keep Power Pages sites secure from initial configuration through ongoing maintenance. Business Value: Security agent empowers makers to set up secure access controls without needing deep security expertise. It uses AI to recommend the right roles and permissions for your data tables. It continuously monitors your site for misconfigurations, helping you reduce risk, ensure compliance, and build customer trust. Enabled for: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

items.title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Optimize resource scheduling - Optimize schedules with Scheduling Operations Agent
items.description: Dispatchers often spend considerable time and energy reviewing and adjusting each technician's schedule as conditions change throughout the workday: A technician has one or more cancellations in the afternoon. To fill the open slots, what requirements optimally keep promise windows, prefer high-priority work, and locate work around the same neighborhoods that the technician is due to travel to? A technician is running over the planned time for the current booking. As a result, they're late for the next booking, and the delay might cascade to subsequent bookings. How do you best adjust the bookings for the remainder of the day? A technician recovers from illness sooner than expected and is now available for work earlier than planned. What's the best way to schedule work for them when they return? A technician’s schedule contains a lot of low-priority work that isn't due for weeks. How can you improve the schedule with work that better meets desired business goals? A technician’s schedule for the day is built manually or with the schedule assistant. How can you rearrange the schedule so that the resource’s travel time is reduced? In each case, the dispatcher needs to assess the situation, determine which business goals apply, and then update the schedule manually, one booking at a time. With this release of the Scheduling Operations Agent, dispatchers can ask Copilot to provide the best schedule for the affected technician. Within seconds, the dispatcher gets a suggested schedule for review and can apply the updates. You can direct Copilot to optimize for the business goal you want, such as maximizing technician usage or work order priority. Copilot intelligently chooses among existing bookings and new unfulfilled work orders based on factors like skillset match, territories, and customer promise windows. Users can access the feature from the Copilot side pane anywhere within the Dynamics 365 Field Service application. Business Value: The Scheduling Operations Agent for Dynamics 365 Field Service enables dispatchers to quickly and easily optimize schedules for technicians as conditions change throughout the workday, so they can significantly improve their productivity. Dispatchers can ask Copilot to optimize schedules and address issues such as traffic delays, double bookings, or last-minute cancellations that often result in conflicts, gaps, or idle time in a technician's schedule. Instruct Copilot to achieve the desired business objective, such as maximizing technician usage or work order priority while considering factors like skillset match, territories, and promised time windows. items.title: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights - Journeys: Improve engagement and message timing with Outreach Optimization Agent

Listen to incoming interactions and adapt the plan in real time : The agent continuously monitors incoming signals, including engagement and non-responsiveness, and adjusts follow-up timing and cadence, or exits the plan based on whether the goal is progressing or has been achieved. Respect quiet times : The agent enforces quiet time settings as a hard constraint, ensuring that messages are never sent outside approved communication windows, even if engagement data suggests otherwise. Scenario A global retail brand uses Outreach Optimization Agent in a seasonal campaign to re-engage customers. Unlike previous efforts with fixed schedules and repeated reminders, the agent creates a smart baseline plan, then adjusts message timing for each customer based on their engagement. It slows or stops follow-ups when customers show interest and spaces out reminders for unresponsive customers, all while respecting quiet times and consent. This leads to better engagement and less message fatigue, with minimal manual intervention.

items.title: Dynamics 365 Commerce: Author Commerce receipt formats with Copilot Cowork

It applies to receipt formats used by Store Commerce point of sale (POS). Users can: Create and adapt formats: Start from an existing format in the modern Receipt designer representation, create a new format, or request changes to an existing target. Edit receipt sections: Modify header, line, and footer content, field positions, alignment, and supported formatting. Translate and personalize content: Translate static labels and add user-supplied text while preserving dynamic fields. Missing business details are identified rather than invented. Check layouts without changing them: Request structural or geometry checks that identify overlaps, width violations, and truncation risks, with findings and suggested remediation. Verify saved changes: Review the resulting format and changes, with saved configuration re-read to confirm the requested update. Creating a format from a source preserves that source. The skill is available automatically to authorized Copilot Cowork users. Users describe the source format and desired outcome, resolve any source or target ambiguity, and review the results. A Commerce administrator ensures appropriate headquarters access and that the source format is available in the modern structured representation. Structural checks do not establish visual appearance, barcode scanability, runtime values, or legal and fiscal compliance. Users review the layout in the Receipt designer and perform appropriate test printing before operational use. The agent automatically groups not only expenses based on the location, but uses intelligence to group all expenses based on the context. Non-trip related expenses keep existing period-based grouping in expense reports.

items.title: Microsoft Teams: AI-powered notes for in-person meetings with Facilitator in Teams Rooms on Windows
items.description: In addition to capturing real-time notes and meeting outcomes during scheduled or hybrid meetings, the Facilitator agent assists you with notes, decisions and actions for in-person meetings in Teams Rooms on Windows. Simply invite Facilitator with one tap of the room console. Meeting notes appear on the front of room display or touch board, are available via meeting recap when shared, and deleted if no one selected. Rest assured no data remains in the room. items.title: Microsoft Dataverse: Enable semantic data understanding for agentic use
items.description: Give AI agents and Copilot a true understanding of your business data — not just raw schema — so they can answer questions accurately with less manual configuration. items.title: Dynamics 365 Field Service: Optimize resource scheduling - Optimize multiple resources with Scheduling Operations Agent
items.description: This release expands the optimization capabilities of the Scheduling Operations Agent to include multiple resources. Create custom goals and weight objectives. Create custom optimization scopes to use with your optimization plans. These capabilities build on the existing public preview of the Scheduling Operations Agent and will be automatically enabled for all organizations that have the agent enabled. Learn more at Scheduling Operations Agent documentation . Business Value: Optimize multiple resources with the Scheduling Operations Agent (SOA). Schedule up to five resources directly from the schedule board or Copilot or perform ad-hoc optimizations for up to 30 resources using an optimization plan. This feature streamlines scheduling, improves efficiency, and supports better resource management. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

items.title: Dynamics 365 Finance: Business performance - MCP for ERP Analytics
items.description: MCP for Analytics provides AI agents with structured access to ERP analytics data and tools. It ensures agents use the same definitions and models as users. items.title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Detect intraday volume spikes with workforce alerts
items.description: Supervisors can create volume spike alerts that compare real-time conversation volume with the forecast linked to a shift plan. When volume remains above forecast for the configured number of intervals, selected recipients receive an in-app notification. The capability includes the following features: Administrators can enable workforce alerts in Copilot Service admin center by going to Workforce management > Intraday management > Workforce alerts . Supervisors can create and manage alerts from Workforce alerts in the Copilot Service workspace site map. Each alert references a shift plan and monitors the queues associated with its linked capacity plan. Supervisors can specify the percentage by which actual volume must exceed forecast volume. Supervisors can specify the number of consecutive intervals during which the deviation must continue before an alert is raised. The forecast determines whether an interval is 15, 30, or 60 minutes. Supervisors can set an expiration date to limit an alert to a campaign, season, or known event. Supervisors can select one or more notification recipients for each alert. Active alerts are evaluated on a recurring schedule. Notifications are sent when the configured threshold and duration are met. Recipients can select a notification to open the alert details. The details include the queue and alert name, detection time, current and forecast volumes, spike percentage, and an interval-by-interval breakdown. Access and prerequisites An administrator must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package from Power Platform admin center. Forecasting and scheduling must be configured. The selected shift plan must have a linked capacity plan and forecast. Real-time conversation data must be available for the monitored queues. Business Value: Contact centers plan staffing based on forecasted demand, but actual demand can change quickly. When conversation volume rises significantly above forecast, queues can grow and service levels can decline before supervisors have time to respond. Workforce alerts help supervisors identify unusual intraday volume changes without continuously monitoring a dashboard. Supervisors define the deviation and duration that represent a volume spike and select who should be notified when those conditions are met. The notification provides information about the spike, including how far actual volume is above forecast and whether the deviation is continuing. Supervisors can use this information to decide whether to shift capacity, offer overtime, or defer offline work while these actions can still help protect the customer experience. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

items.title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Omnichannel customer experiences - Use ML-based sensitive data redaction for human interactions
items.description: Dynamics 365 Contact Center introduces large language model (LLM)-based sensitive data redaction for human-to-human interactions, allowing administrators to automatically redact PCI data shared during live conversations between customers and customer service representatives. The system uses LLMs to identify sensitive data based on conversational context, not just patterns, across both voice and digital channels. When sensitive data such as a credit card number, PIN, or account number is detected, it is replaced with a standardized redaction token (for example, CreditCardNumber:Redacted) before the data is persisted. Redaction is applied consistently across: Conversation transcripts Call recordings Logs and diagnostic data Analytics outputs derived from conversations Administrators can configure which PCI data types are redacted, and the system enforces these policies automatically without requiring representatives to pause recordings or change their workflows. This capability helps ensure that sensitive customer data isn't stored while preserving the non-sensitive conversation context needed for quality assurance, analytics, and operational insights. Business Value: Organizations in regulated industries must prevent sensitive payment data from being stored in call recordings, transcripts, logs, or analytics artifacts. Today, customers rely on manual processes or limited rule-based masking, which increases compliance risk and operational overhead. This feature enables customers to safely use recording, transcription, and AI analytics by ensuring payment card information (PCI) data shared during live conversations between customers and customer service representatives is automatically redacted before storage. As a result, customers can reduce PCI scope, prevent compliance escalations, and confidently adopt advanced contact center capabilities without disrupting agent workflows or customer experience. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

items.title: Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations cross-app: Boost productivity with Copilot - Boost agent performance with optimal tool execution paths in Dynamics 365 ERP MCP
items.description: With the dynamic tools of the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server, large language models often have multiple options for tool-calling sequences to perform an operation or retrieve data. The orchestration can select the tool execution sequence and can include more tool calls than are required. This enhancement to the MCP server improves performance and accuracy of the server response by enabling the server to use optimal tool execution sequences to perform operations with a single point of entry for MCP tools and a semantic index of the available menu items, entities, and actions. Business Value: The Dynamics 365 ERP MCP server now uses a semantic index of target ERP menu items, entities, and actions to improve performance and accuracy of tool calls by optimizing the sequence of tool executions for agentic operations. Enabled for: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

items.title: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: Copilot and AI innovation - Understand forecast accuracy with AI explanations
items.description: By combining forecast results with contextual insights, planners can gain a detailed understanding of the key factors influencing each forecast rather than simply viewing the numbers. This increased transparency builds confidence and supports more informed planning decisions. Key benefits include: See symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) values. View historical data and forecast results in one place. Understand forecast drivers through AI-generated explanations. Gain greater confidence in planning outcomes. Make faster and more informed business decisions. These capabilities help planners spend less time analyzing forecast changes and more time acting. Business Value: Get a clear view of historical data alongside a calculated forecast supported by AI-generated explanations. This feature enhances planners' understanding of each forecast, builds confidence in the results, and enables better planning decisions. Enabled for: Enabled for end users automatically

items.title: Microsoft Dataverse: Microsoft 365 collaboration - Discover, build, customize, and extend with management MCP server
items.description: The management MCP server is a build surface and registry for agent-ready tools available within a customer's environment. It exposes an addressable endpoint where developers and agents can discover, assemble, and deploy MCP servers made from trusted components including connector actions, tools from other MCP servers, and custom APIs. Discover available tools and servers Find MCP servers authored, hosted, or certified by Microsoft Query and explore over 1,470 connectors and their individual actions Discover custom APIs available in your organization or from partner teams Create and customize MCP servers Build new MCP servers by selecting connector actions, APIs, and reusable tools Clone an existing MCP server, such as a Dataverse MCP, and tailor it by adding or removing tools to match your scenario Use MCP servers as modular, scenario-focused endpoints that can be reused across agents Endpoint driven developer experience Accessible as a simple environment scoped URL—no UI required Use in Visual Studio Code, Claude, or any agent or tool that supports HTTP Compose, publish, and maintain MCP servers entirely through API calls Enterprise ready governance and control Enforce data loss prevention (DLP) policies Apply access controls at both the MCP server and individual tool level The management MCP server gives you everything you need to build and scale agents using tools you already trust, no interface required, just secure, extensible control from the systems you already manage. Business Value: The management Model Context Protocol (MCP) server gives developers and system integrators a central API-based foundation to discover and build custom MCP servers. Through a single environment scoped endpoint, teams can find Microsoft certified or internal MCP servers, search across 1,470 connector actions and APIs, and create new or customized MCP servers with the exact tools their agents need. This capability reduces redundant development and enables a flexible, secure path from prototype to production across platforms like Visual Studio Code and Claude. Enabled for: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

items.title: Dynamics 365 Customer Service: Workforce engagement management - Monitor intraday performance against the forecast
items.description: The intraday performance report provides supervisors with an interval-level view of performance against the forecast. In Copilot Service workspace, go to Workforce management to access the report. Compare forecast and actual contact volume and average handle time. Variances appear as values and percentages, making outliers easier to identify. Compare forecast, required, and scheduled staffing levels to identify understaffed and overstaffed intervals. Review service level, occupancy, and schedule adherence alongside volume and staffing data in a single report. View data in 15-, 30-, or 60-minute intervals to match how your organization manages intraday performance. Filter the report by planning group and shift plan to focus on the areas you manage. Access and prerequisites To use Workforce Management capabilities, an administrator must install the Workforce Management for Customer Service package from the Power Platform admin center. Business Value: Contact center forecasts and schedules are built days or weeks in advance, but demand rarely arrives exactly as planned. When volume spikes, handle times run long, or agents are absent, supervisors often don't see the gap until service levels have already slipped and the interval is gone. The intraday performance report closes that gap by showing plan versus actual as the day unfolds. Supervisors can see which intervals are under- or over-staffed and act while there's still time by moving agents between queues, adjusting break and training schedules, or opening overtime only where it's genuinely needed. That protects service level and abandonment targets on the days that matter most, and it curbs the two costs that quietly compound in every contact center: paying for idle capacity in over-forecasted intervals and paying premium rates to recover from under-forecasted ones. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

items.title: Dynamics 365 Finance: Core financials - Enable import of customer payment remittance advice for processing and settlement
items.description: This feature includes the following functionalities: Automated customer payment and remittance advice import, scanning, and mapping using AI processing in the integrated Power Platform environment. Matching remittance advice data with data in Dynamics 365 Finance. Seamless integration of remittance advice details into Dynamics 365 Finance customer payment journals and the settlement process. Reports that provide insights into payment and settlement statuses, outstanding invoices, and overall cash flow. items.title: Dynamics 365 Sales: Seller experiences - Clone and share Sales Development agent configuration across teams
items.description: As a sales leader, you can configure a Sales Development agent once, then share or clone its configuration across your organization. Distribute the agent’s playbook, guidelines, guardrails, and settings to other business units to provide a consistent experience across sales teams. The feature supports these capabilities: Export a configuration : In Teams, ask the source agent to package its configuration into a file. For example, enter Export your configuration. Import a configuration : Attach the exported file to a new agent, then ask the agent to apply the configuration. Create a one-time copy : The copied configuration is a snapshot, not a synchronized connection. Changes made later to the source agent aren’t automatically applied to the target agent. Knowledge sources, such as uploaded documents, FAQs, and URLs, aren’t included in the exported configuration. Add them directly to the target agent after importing the configuration. Business Value: Scaling your sales operations just got easier. Instead of manually configuring each Sales Development agent from scratch, you can now set up an agent once with your organization's best practices and guardrails, then share or clone it across your entire team. This means faster deployment, consistent outreach to prospects, and more time for your sellers to build relationships instead of repetitive work. Whether you're expanding to new markets or rolling out agents across multiple business units, you'll maintain quality and compliance while reducing the time it takes to get your agent up and running. Enabled for: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

items.title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Copilot and AI innovation - Use agentic simulations to evaluate contact center setup
items.description: Agentic simulations are an AI-driven capability of Service Operations Agent that enable organizations to evaluate how their contact center behaves under realistic customer conditions before those conditions occur in production. Administrators define simulation scenarios using natural-language prompts. Agentic simulations then generate realistic synthetic conversations, runs them end-to-end through the configured contact center, and calculates the contact center KPIs. What problems it helps solve Readiness of self-service experiences : Assess how AI agents handle real customer intents, variations in behavior, and edge cases. Effectiveness of assisted service flows : Validate routing, assignment logic, and service representative experience in human-assisted scenarios. Confidence in scale and load readiness : Understand how configurations and operations perform under realistic volume and fix any reliability and latency issues. Preparedness of service representatives : Enable safe practice and evaluation using realistic customer interactions without impacting live customers. Key capabilities Natural-language prompt interface for defining simulation scenarios Simulation of varied customer intents, personas, and behaviors End-to-end execution across AI agents, routing, and configurations Out-of-the-box KPI dashboards and scorecards Reusable and saved prompts, including canned scenarios Safe, pre-production execution with no impact on live customers Agentic simulations are currently available for the voice channel in the English language only. They support flows without Dual-Tone Multi-Frequency (DTMF)-based menu interactions and up to five conversations in a simulation. Business Value: Every contact center decision, such as deploying an AI agent, adjusting routing, onboarding new staff, or preparing for higher volumes, ultimately answers the same question: “Will this work as expected when real customers arrive?” Agentic simulations provide a clear, data-backed answer before changes reach production. By generating realistic customer conversations and running them end-to-end through the contact center, organizations can see how their self-service, assisted service, and operational setup behave under real-world conditions. Instead of relying on assumptions, limited testing, or post-go-live corrections, teams gain measurable insight into experience quality, readiness, and scale. This feature transforms how contact centers operate: Experience quality improves because AI agents and service representatives are evaluated against realistic scenarios. Operational risk decreases because configuration and routing issues are identified early. Time to value accelerates because onboarding, training, and change validation happen faster. Scale becomes predictable because load behavior is understood before demand increases. Agentic simulations turn uncertainty into confidence, helping organizations ship changes faster, train teams better, and deliver consistent customer experiences at scale. Enabled for: Enabled for admins/makers/marketers automatically

items.title: Dynamics 365 Contact Center: Administrator experiences - Use industry templates to set up autonomous contact centers

Users can leverage these templates as a foundation and extend them to meet their specific customer service requirements. These templates enable organizations to rapidly launch autonomous contact centers, reduce implementation complexity, and begin delivering AI-powered customer support with minimal configuration effort. In this release, templates are available for the retail and telecom industries. Business Value: Accelerate the deployment of autonomous contact centers with prebuilt industry templates designed to help organizations get up and running in minutes rather than weeks. These ready-to-use templates reduce the complexity of designing autonomous customer service experiences from scratch, enabling businesses to quickly realize the benefits of AI-powered customer engagement, automated issue resolution, and around-the-clock service availability. items.title: Dynamics 365 Commerce: Enable MCP tools for POS returns

The tools can also explain return eligibility, policy restrictions, and why specific lines may or may not be returnable. They can analyze prior returns and refunds to surface duplicate-refund risk, frequent-return patterns, cross-store return history, or other return-risk indicators. Tool responses provide structured data that host experiences can use to present return details, choices, summaries, and next steps in the experience they build. Customers can use these tools from POS-embedded agents, chat-based copilots, workflow orchestrators, or other agentic surfaces. Customers configure the host surface, authorize the agent or integration to call the tools, and maintain existing Commerce return policies, reason codes, tender rules, and payment configuration.

items.title: Power Apps: Manage model-driven app AI features from consolidated settings
